newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Petroz shares rise on oil find.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Petroz shares rise on oil find.

text.p: Shares in Petroz NL rose almost 10 percent on Thursday on news of a discovery in the Timor Gap which is expected to boost the Elang/Kakatua oilfields.
Petroz closed at A$1.09 a share, up from A$1.00 prior to the announcement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
Petroz said the Kakatua North-1A, operated by the BHP Petroleum unit of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, had encountered a gross hydrocarbon column of about 70 metres.
The well is located on a separate structure 1.1 km to the north of the Kakatua-1 oil discovery in the Timor Sea Zone of Cooperation between Australia and Indonesia.
Analysts said the find in permit ZOCA 91-12 was encouraging as it could be tied in to the Elang/Kakatua development.
Hartley Poynton oil and gas analyst Ann Diamant said the discovery was likely to be towards the upper range of an expected five million to 15 million barrel accumulation.

"It's pretty good news," Diamant said. "None of these structures is very large in that area, but clearly once Elang/Kakatua is up and running if they can add in reserves they can do it very profitably."
BHP Petroluem spokesman Robert Porter said it was too early to determine the commercial significance of the well.
"It is encouraging obviously because it is located quite close to the other wells in the area," he said.
BHP holds 42.417 percent of the well, Santos Ltd 21.426 percent, Indonesia's Inpex Sahul Ltd 21.209 percent, and Petroz 14.948 percent.
Santos said in October that Elang/Kakatua would be developed at a cost of A$90 million, to start production in mid-1988.
